answer: Each agent must stake a unique cryptographic token that is bound to a physical‑world proof of presence, such as a signed beacon from a sensor network deployed in a remote grove. The network issues reward lanterns that vest linearly over weeks; a new island of identities can only claim the first lantern after paying the full stake, while each additional claim incurs an exponential fee that grows with the number of simultaneous vesting streams. An attacker therefore spends real collateral and time for every fake node, making a Sybil flood prohibitively costly.
